answer: A device proves it shares my mains supply by recording the 50Hz hum for ninety seconds, then cross-correlating its phase against a public grid monitor, where the matching signal must clear a published threshold before any identity is issued. A cedar pole outside my house carries the same feeder, so the hum matches only there, and the atlas of grid segments shows each one hums with its own phase, forcing a farm to tap every claimed segment in hardware.
